name: A194259(n) - n, where A194259(n) is the number of distinct prime factors of p(1)*p(2)*...*p(n) and p(n) is the n-th partition number.
comment: Schinzel and Wirsing proved that a(n) > C*log n - n, for any positive constant C < 1/log 2 and all large n. In fact, it appears that a(n) > 0 for all n > 115.
It also appears that a(n) >= a(n-1), for all n > 97, so that some prime factor of p(n) does not divide p(1)*p(2)*...*p(n-1).
link: Alois P. Heinz and Giovanni Resta, Table of n, a(n) for n = 1..10000 (first 2000 terms from Alois P. Heinz)
A. Schinzel and E. Wirsing, Multiplicative properties of the partition function, Proc. Indian Acad. Sci., Math. Sci. (Ramanujan Birth Centenary Volume), 97 (1987), 297-303; alternative link.
mathematica: a[n_] := PrimeNu[Product[PartitionsP[k], {k, 1, n}]] - n; Table[a[n], {n, 1, 116}] (* _Jean-François Alcover_, Jan 28 2014 *)
